rules.name: Exposed Docker Daemon Socket
rules.description: Exposing /var/run/docker.sock allows containers full root access to the host Docker daemon, leading to potential host takeover.
rules.mitigation: Avoid mounting docker.sock. Use a scoped API proxy or eBPF/kernel-based drivers (e.g., Falco) for monitoring.

rules.name: Container Running as Root
rules.description: Running containers as root increases the impact of privilege escalation attacks.
rules.mitigation: Define a non-root user in the Dockerfile using USER instruction or specify user in Docker Compose.

rules.name: Unnecessary Linux Capabilities
rules.description: Excessive Linux capabilities broaden the attack surface. Using --privileged grants all host capabilities.
rules.mitigation: Drop unneeded capabilities with 'cap_drop: [ALL]' and selectively add required ones with 'cap_add'. Never use privileged mode.

rules.name: In-Container Privilege Escalation Allowed
rules.description: Processes inside the container can gain new privileges via setuid or setgid binaries.
rules.mitigation: Set security option 'no-new-privileges:true' in your container runtime or Compose configuration.

rules.name: Missing Resource Limits
rules.description: Lack of CPU, memory, restart, or process limits makes the host vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) attacks.
rules.mitigation: Define 'cpus', 'memory', restart limits, and ulimits (nofile, nproc) in your container specification.

rules.name: Writable Root Filesystem
rules.description: A writable root filesystem enables attackers to modify application files or write malicious binaries.
rules.mitigation: Set 'read_only: true' and use tmpfs mounts for temporary directory writes.
